newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA'S HOWARD SAYS GROWTH OUTLOOK STRONG.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA'S HOWARD SAYS GROWTH OUTLOOK STRONG.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that the outlook for economic growth was very strong.
"The outlook for growth is very strong," Howard told reporters.
"I don't favour some broad-based budget stimulus. We don't need that," he said.
Since winning power in March 1996, the Liberal-National coalition government has implemented savings which will eventually be worth about six percent of budget spending.
Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane, reflecting on subdued inflationary pressures, said on Tuesday that Australian GDP could grow at an annual rate of 4.5 percent or more for the next few years.
The government has projected 3.75 percent economic growth in the 1997/98 fiscal year from July 1.
Australian GDP growth decelerated last year.
The economy grew only 2.4 percent between the March quarters of 1996 and 1997.
Its long-run trend growth rate is around 3.2 percent.
